text:
carla: quick note from an onboarding run: saw the sample-app emit two different reqids for what is clearly one user flow and one of the logs exposed an email. Repro attached below.

ishaan: ouch. is this the express retry-replay pattern again? paste the raw lines + how you wired telemetry.

carla: sanitized lines from node sample (express + retry-replay):\n```\nINFO 2026-06-12T14:02:10Z req_id=run42 user=pat@example.com step=auth.start\nINFO 2026-06-12T14:02:11Z req_id=run42 step=auth.retry attempt=1\nINFO 2026-06-12T14:02:12Z req_id=run42-final user=pat@example.com step=auth.finish\n```
first two look redacted/clean, last one leaked the email and has a different req_id. sdk init in sample app:\n```js\nTelemetry.configure({ hooks: [otelAttach, redactHook, sampler] })\n```
I suspect the retry handler creates a fresh context/span and emits after attach-time hooks already ran.

mei: is redactHook attached to span creation or to the logger output? If attach-only it could be missed on replays.

ishaan: yep. attach-time redaction works for the common path but not for replay/re-emitted records. We saw similar with streaming replays where final emit had additional fields.

carla: i tried a small mod in the sample app to move redaction to the output pipeline and it stopped the leak:\n```js\nlogger.on('record', (r) => { if (!r._redacted) { redactPII(r); r._redacted = true } });\n```
makes redaction idempotent and safe for re-emits. perf feels fine on a small run but we need a benchmark.

sdk-bot: opened ticket DE-6120: "node SDK: req_id drift + missed redaction on retry/replay path" -> https://jira/redwood/DE-6120 :memo:

mei: two things to consider: (1) defaulting node SDK to emit-time redaction, with an opt-in legacy attach-mode flag; (2) add a cheap boolean marker so repeated emits are cheap. Also add integration tests for replay flows.

ishaan: agree. additionally, we should verify OpenTelemetry context propagation: if retry spawns a new span, the req_id changed. We should either make retry preserve the original req id or ensure logs are correlated via a stable request fingerprint (e.g., incoming request id header).

carla: for the sample app, the middleware drops the header when it re-dispatches. quick fix is to reattach the original header when re-dispatching. but robust fix should be at SDK level.

mei: plan proposal: 1) add integration test that simulates express retry/replay and streaming replays asserting single stable req_id and zero raw emails; 2) change node SDK redact hook to run on final logger emit by default with legacy attach-mode behind a flag; 3) add _redacted marker to avoid duplicate work; 4) add microbench numbers to PR; 5) ship 0.12.4-canary and monitor PII alerting dashboards.

ishaan: i'll draft the test harness and a microbench. can you own the PR for the SDK change, @mei?

mei: yep. i'll include migration notes and a note in the SDK changelog about the new default and the compat flag. also will add a unit that simulates double-emits to validate the marker logic.

carla: added repro artifacts to DE-6120 and a short shell script to repro locally. cc @oncall for visibility.

ishaan: thanks. tiny follow-up: check python sampleapp too; python logging pipeline is slightly different and might already be emit-time redaction (if so, call that out in release notes).

mei: good call. i'll run a quick python smoke to confirm. if python is fine we limit the change to node.

carla: :thumbsup: will update the ticket with a checklist and link to the sample app patch.
